findings.issue: Step 4 prescribes seeding the group-name input with the value resolved through the Task 05 helper (`resolve(storedTitle, defaultLabel)`), i.e. a group that has never been renamed shows 'Focus' as the input VALUE, not as a placeholder. Three consequences follow, none of which the task's own Acceptance Criteria would catch: (a) the placeholder specified in the same step is dead — it can never be seen for a default-named group, contradicting user-spec 0011 line ~101 ('Пока поле пустое, в нём серым показывается дефолтное название группы') and Scenario 2 step 3; (b) any Save — even one that only toggles visibility — writes 'Focus'/'Backlog'/... into `Group.title` for all six groups, so switching the plugin language stops translating group names, contradicting user-spec Scenario 1 step 5 and line 172 ('Пока название дефолтное, перевод работает как прежде'); (c) Task 06 treats any non-empty `title` as 'renamed' and swaps the semantic empty-state hint for the neutral one (task-06 edge case: 'Group renamed to exactly its default name → non-empty stored title, so the neutral hint appears'), so after the first save every empty group loses its semantic hint. Tech-spec Decision 4 carries the same wording, so the defect originates there.
findings.fix: Bind the input's value to the RAW stored title (`board.groups[id].title`, possibly empty) and `$groupLabels[groupId]` to `placeholder`. The Task 05 resolve helper belongs to display sites (Task 06), not to the editable input — do not call it for the input value. Add an acceptance criterion: 'Opening board settings and saving without editing any name leaves every `Group.title` empty; group names still translate after a language switch.' Reconcile tech-spec Decision 4 with the same correction.

findings.issue: TDD Anchor claims the case `перестановка разрывает пару` is 'the case that would fail if the ordered array were not actually reaching the function'. That is not true: the test calls the pure `computeGroupClasses` directly with a hand-built array, so it cannot observe whether `BoardLayout.svelte` feeds it `board.groupOrder` — the same task states the component is untestable here (`vitest.config.ts` sets `environment: 'node'`, no DOM library). The rationale gives false confidence that the central wiring of the task is covered.
findings.fix: Reword the anchor: the three cases prove `computeGroupClasses` is order-agnostic, nothing more. State explicitly that the wiring (board.groupOrder → visibleGroups → classes + order) has no automated coverage until Task 10, and that `npx playwright test tests/e2e/0007-dynamic-layout.spec.ts` plus the manual harness check are the only gates in this task.

findings.issue: The two markup outputs this task introduces — the inline `order` value and `data-group-container` — have no automated assertion in this task. A missing `data-group-container` surfaces two waves later in Task 09; a wrong `order` value surfaces only in Task 10 (wave 6), and only the manual harness check in Verification Steps would catch it earlier. This is a deliberate deferral (tech-spec Decision 12), but it leaves the task's central acceptance criteria machine-unverifiable at the moment of hand-off.
findings.fix: Either accept explicitly (note in Verification Steps that ACs 3, 4 and 6 are verified manually in this task), or add one cheap Playwright assertion in an existing file scope — e.g. that six `[data-group-container]` elements exist and their computed `order` values form a dense 1..N sequence — to give the wave a machine gate.

findings.issue: `depends_on: ["03", "06"]` does not list Task 01, but step 7 extends `tests/unit/boardLayoutUtils.test.ts`, which does not exist yet — today the file lives at `src/ui/boardLayoutUtils.test.ts` and is not even collected by vitest (`include: ['tests/unit/**/*.test.ts']`). Task 01 performs the move. The dependency is satisfied transitively (07 → 03 → 01) and by wave ordering (0 → 1 → 3), so it is not blocking, but it is not declared.
findings.fix: Add "01" to `depends_on` of Task 07, or note in Details that the dependency is transitive through Task 03.

findings.issue: Details attribute the comment 'Uses title text to find the header since [data-group-id] is only in the body' to the `COLLAPSIBLE_GROUP_LABELS` constant. In the real file that sentence is line 97 of `tests/e2e/helpers.ts`, part of the JSDoc block of `expandGroup` (lines 95–98); the constant's own comment is line 89, '// EN labels for collapsible groups (backlog and completed)'. findings.issue: The description says reusing `data-group-id` on the wrapper 'would break twelve strict-mode assertions'; the same 'twelve' appears in Task 07 Edge cases with an explicit list of line numbers — `helpers.ts:100`, `0006-group-visibility.spec.ts:95, 108, 112, 120, 199, 200, 240, 284, 285`, `core.spec.ts:245, 248, 252`. findings.issue: Acceptance criterion 'that attribute name is used nowhere else in the codebase' is unsatisfiable as literally written once Task 09 lands, since Task 09 introduces `data-settings-group` locators throughout `tests/e2e/`. The task's own Verification Steps already scope the check correctly (`grep -rn "data-settings-group" src/`).
findings.fix: Scope the criterion to `src/`: 'the attribute name appears nowhere else under `src/`'.

findings.issue: Step 10 normalizes titles at the store boundary (Decision 7) but writes `groupOrder` verbatim, with no validation. Task 03's sanitizer only runs at load, so an order arriving malformed (missing or duplicated id) would leave the board scrambled for the rest of the session and be repaired only on next start. Today the popup's local copy is a permutation by construction, so this is latent rather than live.
findings.fix: Either reuse Task 03's exported order sanitizer inside `updateBoard` alongside the title normalization, or state in Details that the store boundary deliberately trusts the caller for `groupOrder` and record the reason.

findings.issue: All three tasks list `docs/features/0011-feat-group-customization/0011-feat-group-customization-decisions.md` under Context Files as material to read, but the file does not exist in the feature directory. It is only written at Post-completion, so an executor of the first task in a wave has nothing to read.
findings.fix: Mark the decisions log in Context Files as 'created during execution — may not exist yet', or create an empty stub during decomposition.
